mentions.name: Real-time tensor processing compiler
mentions.description: This compiler targets real-time tensor processing workloads such as DSP and ML: programs written in a fully general language like LISP or Haskell are compiled from lambda calculus for fast, reliable execution, so code that looks like DSP/ML math compiles and runs optimally with on-budget execution guaranteed by construction, without explicitly modeling the lower levels of the machine.
mentions.problem: Writing real-time DSP/ML programs normally requires explicitly modeling the lower levels of the machine to guarantee execution on budget.
mentions.source_excerpt: A compiler for real-time tensor processing (arbitrary DSP, ML). In something like LISP or Haskell, the goal is to compile lambda calculus for fast/reliable execution—as such, you can express a program in a fully general language that can represent any computation and execute it without explicitly modeling the lower levels of the machine.
